    Sizes and structure

    The box is 600 wide x 860 high x 520 deep (mm), in 18 mm board. A 22 inch monitor fits inside with about 35 mm spare on each side for cables and air.

    Structure rules

    • Board. 18 mm plywood for the sides, base and monitor board. MDF is acceptable for other panels, but pre-drill because its edges split.
    • Battens everywhere. Glue and screw a 25 x 25 mm batten inside both sides along the line of every cross panel, set back 18 mm so the panel sits flush. Screw each panel to its battens about every 150 mm.
    • Full back panel. Glued and screwed on all four edges. It stops the box leaning sideways. Keep the door opening at least 60 mm in from every edge.
    • Monitor on its own board. The monitor bolts through its four VESA holes to the plywood board, which sits on battens on both sides. Comparable monitors weigh 2.2 to 3 kg.
    • Second support. A small ledge under the monitor's bottom edge, so the bolts are not the only thing holding it.
    • Acrylic carries nothing. The screen cover only hides the monitor frame. It must not press on the screen.
    • Air. A slot low in the back for cool air, vents high in the back for warm air.
    • Weight. About 25 kg finished, estimated from the panel areas. Two people lift it, and the table under it must be solid.

    Power

    The whole box runs from one wall socket. A single mains cable enters at the back and feeds a power strip inside.

    Socket 1

    Monitor adapter, then the monitor. Comparable 22 inch monitors use 12 V, 2 A. Confirm on the Blisbond label.

    Socket 2

    USB charger, then the X6 game stick, the marquee LED strip and the fan.

    Sockets 3 and 4

    Spare. One is kept for the Snapdash computer when the photo game is added.

    • X6 power. Its listing does not say how it is powered. Sticks of this kind normally take USB power. Confirm on the unit before buying the charger.
    • Webcam. Its USB cable drops through the top and is left coiled inside, ready for the Snapdash computer. The X6 does not use it.
    • Master switch. The switch on the power strip turns the whole box on and off. Reach it through the rear door.
    • No mains wiring by hand. Use the adapters as supplied. Do not cut or join their cables. An electrician fits any switched inlet.
    • Cable exit. The mains cable leaves through a grommet in the back and is clamped inside.
    • Monitor after a power cut. Check that the monitor turns itself back on when power returns. If it does not, its power button must stay reachable.
    • Controllers. The listing does not say what batteries they take. Keep spares in the box.

    Build steps

    1. Test the electronics on a tablePlug the X6 stick into the monitor's HDMI port, power both, pair the two controllers and play a game.
    2. Measure the monitorRemove its stand and fill in the measurement table. Note where the HDMI and power sockets are.
    3. Cut the two sidesMark the profile on one 520 x 860 mm board and cut it. Clamp it to the second board, trace, cut, then sand both together so they match.
    4. Cut the cross panelsAll 564 mm wide. Label each one in pencil.
    5. Make the openings while the panels are flatBack: door opening, vent slots, low air slot, cable exit. Top: camera cable hole. Speaker panel: sound holes.
    6. Fix the battensLay both sides down as a mirrored pair. Glue and screw battens along every panel line, 18 mm in from the edge.
    7. Join base and back to the sidesGlue and screw. Measure both diagonals of the back. When they are equal the box is square.
    8. Add the top, angled strip and front panelDry-fit first, then glue and screw.
    9. Add the control shelf and speaker panel
    10. Fit the monitor board and test-fit the monitorSet the board at the screen angle, about 7 degrees back. Bolt the monitor on, check the picture is centred in the opening, then take it off again.
    11. Finish the woodFill screw heads and sand. Paint black wherever the skin will not cover: top, back, edges and the screen surround.
    12. Refit the monitor and add the ledgeThe ledge sits under the monitor's bottom edge.
    13. Fit the acrylicScreen cover with its black border, then the marquee face with the LED strip behind it.
    14. Install the electronicsPower strip and adapters on the base. X6 stick into the monitor's HDMI port with its controller receiver. Clip the webcam on the top front and drop its cable through the hole. Tie the cables in neat runs.
    15. Apply the skinBoth sides, the control shelf and the front panel. Work from the centre outward to push out air.
    16. Door, lock, feet, then a two-hour closed testPlay with the door shut to confirm the controllers still connect through the wood. If the inside gets hot, add the fan.

    Final checks

    • The game menu appears by itself when the power strip is switched on
    • The monitor comes back on by itself after power is cut and restored
    • Both controllers work from 2 m away with the rear door closed
    • Spare batteries are in the box
    • Nothing inside is hot to the touch after two hours closed
    • The mains cable is clamped inside and no adapter cable is stretched
    • The box does not rock on the table and has no sharp edges
    • The rear door locks

    Product 2 runs the Snapdash photo game, which is not built yet. The hardware can be built now, but it has nothing to show until the game exists.

    Part drawings

    Each face of the case with its size and openings, in mm. Positions are measured from the left edge and the bottom edge. These are my proposed positions, so adjust them to the case and connectors you buy.

    Power

    One supply

    A 5 V 2.5 A micro USB power supply feeds the Pi. The Pi powers the hub, the webcam and the gamepad.

    The screen

    The venue's screen or projector has its own power. Sound goes to it over the HDMI cable.

    Internet

    The box needs 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi to reach the character server. Bring a hotspot if the venue's Wi-Fi is unreliable.

    • Power cuts. A Pi can corrupt its memory card if power is cut while it runs. Plan a read-only system as a software step.

    Build steps

    1. Test the electronics on a tableConnect the Pi, hub, webcam and gamepad to any screen and confirm each one works.
    2. Choose the caseLay the Pi, hub and cables inside before buying or cutting, to confirm the 220 x 150 x 70 mm size.
    3. Mark and drill the openingsBack: HDMI, power and two USB. Lid: webcam cable hole. Sides: vent slots.
    4. Fix the Pi and hubOn standoffs or foam pads. Nothing should rest on the board.
    5. Fit the back connectorsPanel-mount extension cables for HDMI and USB, each one clamped so plugging in does not strain the Pi.
    6. Mount the webcam on the lidOn its tilt clip at the front edge, cable through the hole to the hub.
    7. Apply the skinThe artwork crop on the lid and the logo on the front, as a printed vinyl sticker.
    8. Test on a big screen or projectorCheck the picture fills the screen, sound plays through it, and the Wi-Fi connects.

    Final checks

    • The box starts by itself when power is connected
    • The webcam sees a player standing 1.5 to 2 m away
    • The gamepad cable cannot be pulled out of the box
    • The picture and sound work on both a TV and a projector
    • The box is only warm, not hot, after two hours

    Printables

    Make every printed piece for either product from your own artwork and logo. The files are built in your browser. Nothing you upload leaves this device.

    1. Choose the product
    2. Upload the artworkOne picture that fills the panels. Use a large file: about 3,200 x 5,200 pixels covers an arcade side panel at print quality.
    3. Upload the logoA PNG with a transparent background works best. It is placed on the marquee, on both side panels and on the Mini's front.
    4. Check the previewsEach piece is shown with 10 mm of extra artwork on every edge. The pink line is where the printer cuts.
    5. Download each fileFiles are PNG at 150 dots per inch, at full print size.
    6. Send them to the printerAsk for laminated vinyl for the sides, shelf, front and the Mini. Ask for backlit film for the arcade marquee, because it is lit from behind.
    7. ApplyClean the surface, peel a little backing at a time and press from the centre outward to push out air.

    Until you upload your own, the previews use a small crop of Skin 01, which is too low in resolution to print. The side panels crop the picture to fit, so check that nothing important sits under the logo or outside the cut line.

    Risks

    • Late parts. Online delivery can take several of the six days. Buy over the counter where possible.
    • Skin printing. Send the artwork on day 2 so the print is back by day 6. If it is late, the box can run in plain black.
    • Paint drying on day 4. If time runs short, drop the marquee light before anything else.
    • Product 2 has no game yet. Its four days cover hardware only.
